summary: The TypeScript Playwright code compiles and runs with correct use of async/await and Playwright APIs. Locators are correctly used with asynchronous assertions. However, there are some selector concerns such as reliance on assumed roles (form with name, combobox with name) without guarantee these exist, and generic selectors like 'textarea' or 'button[type="submit"]'. Some assertion texts are generic or placeholders (e.g., confirmation message detection), reducing reliability. Test titles preserve testCaseId and cover all GENERATED cases. No compilation or API misuse found.

issues.description: Selectors like getByRole('form', { name: /contact/i }) and getByRole('combobox', { name: /subject/i }) assume accessibility roles and names that may not exist in the tested page, potentially causing flakiness.
issues.recommendation: Verify the accessibility tree of the target page to ensure these roles and names exist, or use more robust selectors combining attributes or test IDs.

issues.description: Assertions checking visible error or confirmation messages rely on generic text patterns such as /confirmation message/i or /must be at least 50 characters/i which may not match actual messages on the page.
issues.recommendation: Update assertions to match exact visible text in the application to ensure test reliability.

issues.description: Usage of generic selectors such as 'textarea' or 'button[type="submit"]' may match unexpected elements if page structure changes.
issues.recommendation: Consider using more specific locators, e.g., by label text or data-test attributes to increase stability.

recommendations: Confirm that all role and name selectors correspond to real attributes in the tested page.
Replace generic error and confirmation message patterns with exact expected texts.
Use test-specific attributes or more descriptive selectors to avoid ambiguity.
Add navigation validation such as URL checks or wait for specific page states after navigation or submission.
